data.gender_notes: Charuvrata is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Charuvrata is derived from the Sanskrit language, where 'Charu' means desire and 'Vrata' means vow or promise. This name symbolizes the fulfillment of a deep desire or the keeping of a sacred vow. The name Charuvrata carries the meaning “Desire Fulfilled” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Charuvrata usually hope their child will grow to embody desire fulfilled and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name that embodies the strength and determination to fulfill one's deepest desires and promises.
data.etymology: Charuvrata belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire Fulfilled.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Charuvrata total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

This is an essential value in Hindu traditions, where fulfilling one's duties and obligations is highly revered. Charuvrata emphasizes the importance of maintaining personal and spiritual commitments, which can bring success and happiness in life.

Charuvrata also serves as a reminder of the importance of introspection and self-reflection in the pursuit of spiritual growth. historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata mentions a Charuvrata, a chariot belonging to the Pandava Bhima. This chariot was a gift from Indra to Bhima, who used it during the Kurukshetra War.
Another reference to Charuvrata is found in the Puranas, where it is described as a special kind of ritually purified chariot used in various yajnas (sacrifices) and processions for the deity Vishnu.
